scope: Meaning drafts in batches 16–23, 78 meanings and 234 authored questions

corrections.reason: With only one mentioned man, celui-là could also refer to him. Specified two men in order so the latter, celui-ci, is unambiguous.
The vague les autres could also denote his traveling companions. Replaced it with inconnus and made his own group explicit.

note: Checked source spans, selected workwide contexts, contextual meanings and each three-band choice set for the remaining chapter I drafts. Corrected two ambiguous choice sets. The first 228 chapter I draft meanings have a recorded source-and-question review; eight later corrections are recorded in QA04, but final shared-identity mapping and publication are pending.

items.reviewNote: Source sense: Ce qui fait une très-jolie proportion names what the preceding calculation results in. This is not the past participle fait, nor all the later verbal faire contexts. The three question answers, in band order, are "yields", "fait", "fait"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Devint depuis marks what Pascal became afterward in the old narrative usage. The later depuis la tête jusqu’aux pieds marks spatial extent, so this is a contextual subset. The Académie française third edition records depuis used independently as a time adverb: https://www.dictionnaire-academie.fr/article/A3D0611 . The three question answers, in band order, are "subsequently", "depuis", "depuis"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Sentant l’hérésie describes propositions that seem to contain heretical doctrine in the censor’s judgment. It does not describe an actual physical smell or the reflexive feeling oneself. The three question answers, in band order, are "suggest heresy", "sentant", "sentant"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Mit les femmes de son côté means won the women to his side in the dispute, not the published discourse expression pour son côté meaning for his part. The three question answers, in band order, are "on his side", "côté", "côté"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The author is ordered not to present himself at court for eight hundred years. This is physical/social presence, not seeming or looking a certain way. The three question answers, in band order, are "appear there", "paraître", "paraître"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Eight hundred years is the satirically long period of exile from court, not a measure of distance. The three question answers, in band order, are "years", "années", "années"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Médiocrement affligé means not very upset by banishment from a quarrelsome court; it expresses degree of distress, not a judgment of mediocre skill. The three question answers, in band order, are "only somewhat", "médiocrement", "médiocrement"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The court was filled with petty quarrels and small-minded behavior, explaining why exile did not upset him. The three question answers, in band order, are "full of", "remplie", "remplie"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: He composes a mocking song against the censor; the word names a sung composition rather than a book or speech. The three question answers, in band order, are "song", "chanson", "chanson"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Fort plaisante describes the teasing satirical song against the censor, not an ordinary claim that the legal punishment was pleasant. The three question answers, in band order, are "amusing", "plaisante", "plaisante"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Celui-ci first points back to the muphti and later to a just-mentioned philosopher. It is one hyphenated pronoun, not two mastery items. The three question answers, in band order, are "this one just mentioned", "celui-ci", "celui-ci"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The Sirian begins traveling from planet to planet; the Saturnian’s companion later leaves to travel with a giant. Both involve journeys. The three question answers, in band order, are "travel", "voyager", "voyager"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Pour achever de se former l’esprit et le cœur means developing his intellect and feelings through travel, not molding a physical object. The three question answers, in band order, are "develop his mind", "former", "former"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Those who travel only by post chaise or berline are compared with the giant’s unusual conveyances. The three question answers, in band order, are "travel", "voyagent", "voyagent"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The narrator repeatedly calls Earth a little heap of mud, a satirical image for the planet. All three workwide uses have this meaning. The three question answers, in band order, are "heap", "tas", "tas"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Nous ne concevons rien au delà de nos usages criticizes our inability to imagine unfamiliar ways of life. The three question answers, in band order, are "can imagine", "concevons", "concevons"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Au delà de nos usages means beyond our customs; the later au delà de nos besoins similarly exceeds a limit. The selected edition prints au delà without a hyphen. The three question answers, in band order, are "beyond", "delà", "delà"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The traveler knew the laws of gravitation and attractive and repulsive forces exceptionally well, not merely recognized their names. The three question answers, in band order, are "knew", "connaissait", "connaissait"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: He knows gravitation marvelously well and uses that knowledge in travel; the adverb praises the degree of his understanding. The three question answers, in band order, are "extremely well", "merveilleusement", "merveilleusement"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: A ray of sunlight helps his motion; later a microscope helps him see. The two à l’aide de uses describe an aid or instrument. The three question answers, in band order, are "with the help of", "aide", "aide"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Ne s’embarrassa guère de la mocking song: the censor hardly troubled himself about it. The three question answers, in band order, are "was bothered by", "embarrassa", "embarrassa"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Il s’en servait concerns using celestial forces in travel, not serving a person. The three question answers, in band order, are "used them", "servait", "servait"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Par la commodité d’une comète means using the convenient opportunity or means supplied by a comet, not bodily comfort. Historical Académie: https://www.dictionnaire-academie.fr/article/A4C1715 The three question answers, in band order, are "convenient means", "commodité", "commodité"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Lui et les siens denotes Micromégas and his companions; later lui et les siens denotes a captain and his soldiers. The three question answers, in band order, are "his companions", "siens", "siens"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The bird flitting from branch to branch is the comparison for travel between globes. The three question answers, in band order, are "bird", "oiseau", "oiseau"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The comparison describes a bird flying lightly from branch to branch. The three question answers, in band order, are "flits", "voltige", "voltige"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Both je suis obligé de statements assert the narrator must concede or ask something. Feminine obligée later is a separate mastery surface. The three question answers, in band order, are "compelled to", "obligé", "obligé"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: La voie lactée est semée d’étoiles: stars are scattered through it, not literally planted. The three question answers, in band order, are "strewn with", "semée", "semée"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Le ciel empyrée is the supposed highest heaven; the narrator disputes Derham’s claim to have seen it through a telescope. Historical Académie: https://www.dictionnaire-academie.fr/article/A5E0649 The three question answers, in band order, are "highest heaven", "empyrée", "empyrée"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The narrator uses the honorific for Derham and later for a scholar, archbishop, and father, sometimes with irony. The three question answers, in band order, are "distinguished", "illustre", "illustre"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Derham is identified by his clerical role; do not interpret as a secular secretary. Historical Académie: https://www.dictionnaire-academie.fr/article/A4V0372 The three question answers, in band order, are "clergyman", "vicaire", "vicaire"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Derham se vante d’avoir vu le heaven: the narrator treats his claimed feat with irony. The three question answers, in band order, are "boasts", "vante", "vante"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Au bout de sa lunette refers to Derham’s astronomical viewing instrument, not spectacles. The three question answers, in band order, are "telescope", "lunette", "lunette"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Ce n’est pas que je prétende que… is a disavowal of claiming Derham was wrong. The later pretends to a fétu is a claim of entitlement, reserved separately. The three question answers, in band order, are "claim", "prétende", "prétende"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: À Dieu ne plaise rejects the idea he would accuse Derham of poor observation. Chapter II plaise means please and remains unassigned. Historical Académie: https://www.dictionnaire-academie.fr/article/A4P1253 The three question answers, in band order, are "heaven forbid", "plaise", "plaise"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Micromégas is called an observer both here and when perceiving tiny humans in chapter VI. The three question answers, in band order, are "observer", "observateur", "observateur"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The narrator says he does not wish to contradict anyone after contesting Derham’s sighting. The three question answers, in band order, are "contradict", "contredire", "contredire"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Après avoir bien tourné precedes arrival on Saturn: Micromégas has traveled around, not physically spun in place. The three question answers, in band order, are "traveled around", "tourné", "tourné"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Quelque accoutumé qu’il fût à voir des choses nouvelles: despite habitual exposure, Saturn’s smallness still provokes a smile. The three question answers, in band order, are "used to", "accoutumé", "accoutumé"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Des choses nouvelles means unfamiliar things; later des nouvelles is a noun for news, explicitly outside this draft. The three question answers, in band order, are "new", "nouvelles", "nouvelles"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Le sourire de supériorité comes from the Sirian viewing Saturnians as tiny, a judgment the narrative challenges. The three question answers, in band order, are "superiority", "supériorité", "supériorité"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The smile escapes even the wisest: it occurs despite their better judgment. The three question answers, in band order, are "slips out involuntarily", "échappe", "échappe"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The smile occurs sometimes even among wise people, as later the dwarf judges too quickly sometimes. The three question answers, in band order, are "sometimes", "quelquefois", "quelquefois"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Aux plus sages and later du petit nombre des sages both designate people of sound judgment, not merely a well-behaved child. The three question answers, in band order, are "wisest people", "sages", "sages"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Ce pays-là refers to Saturn and later to the imagined land where nothing is lacking; the suffix points to that place. The three question answers, in band order, are "that place", "pays-là", "pays-là"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: After a measure or near a number, environ marks approximation; the workwide exact-form occurrences share this degree-of-precision sense. The three question answers, in band order, are "approximately", "environ", "environ"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: He mocked the small Saturnians a little before coming to respect their intelligence. The three question answers, in band order, are "made fun of them", "moqua", "moqua"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The Italian musician’s mockery of Lulli’s music is the cultural comparison. The three question answers, in band order, are "musician", "musicien", "musicien"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The musician is Italian; the comparison stages a cultural disagreement about Lulli’s music in France. The three question answers, in band order, are "from Italy", "italien", "italien"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Lulli’s music is what the Italian musician finds laughable in the narrator’s comparison. The three question answers, in band order, are "music", "musique", "musique"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Le livre lui fit quelques affaires: publication caused him trouble. Other fit contexts, including composing a song, need different senses. The three question answers, in band order, are "caused", "fit", "fit"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: L’auteur eut ordre de ne paraître: a prohibition was issued to him. Existing possession/auxiliary avoir may be reusable only after contextual signoff; do not silently assign from spelling. The three question answers, in band order, are "was given an order", "eut", "eut"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Il fit une chanson means he composed a song. It is distinct from the trouble-causing fit and the travel he undertook; published perform-activity identity needs shared-sense review. The three question answers, in band order, are "composed", "fit", "fit"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: A chaise de poste used horses exchanged at posting stations, an eighteenth-century travel conveyance, not the modern mail office. Historical Académie: https://www.dictionnaire-academie.fr/article/A5P1691 The three question answers, in band order, are "post-horse relay travel", "poste", "poste"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Il allait de globe en globe describes movement, not the published imminent futur proche sense of allait. The three question answers, in band order, are "went", "allait", "allait"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: À travers les étoiles and à travers un microscope indicate passage between or through, unlike the published de travers askew sense. Both workwide uses share this locution. The three question answers, in band order, are "through", "travers", "travers"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Le ciel empyrée and un animal vu dans le ciel refer to the heavens, not the published providence sense; juste Ciel is an exclamation and remains separate. The three question answers, in band order, are "sky", "ciel", "ciel"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Quelque accoutumé qu’il fût and later quelque système qu’ils fissent concede a condition without changing the result. Other workwide quelque uses mean some or an unspecified amount. Historical Académie: https://www.dictionnaire-academie.fr/article/A4Q0079 The three question answers, in band order, are "however accustomed", "quelque", "quelque"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Il ne put se défendre de sourire means he could not prevent himself from smiling. Published protect sense does not cover this reflexive construction. The three question answers, in band order, are "keep himself from", "défendre", "défendre"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Car enfin Saturne… introduces justification, not a chronological ending. Historical examples of Car enfin in Académie: https://www.dictionnaire-academie.fr/article/A3E0600 The three question answers, in band order, are "after all", "enfin", "enfin"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Se met à rire means begins to laugh. Draft this present surface for review against published sns_fr_mettre_reflexive_begin under mit, preserving its old mastery and quizzes. The current published met:put identity is wrong here; no published mutation. The three question answers, in band order, are "begins", "met", "met"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: He realizes that intelligent beings need not be tall. The three question answers, in band order, are "understood", "comprit", "comprit"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: All exact-form uses concern speed of thought, movement or judgment; their objects and attitudes differ but speed is shared. The three question answers, in band order, are "quickly", "vite", "vite"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Un être pensant and un être aussi imperceptible refer to individual beings. Infinitive être and Être éternel in the sense of God remain outside this contextual subset. The three question answers, in band order, are "being", "être", "être"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: He became acquainted with the Saturnians after astonishing them. The three question answers, in band order, are "became acquainted", "familiarisa", "familiarisa"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Saturniens is a demonym for the planet’s inhabitants, learnable vocabulary rather than a personal name. Preserve printed capital and plural surface. The three question answers, in band order, are "inhabitants of Saturn", "Saturniens", "Saturniens"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Il lia une étroite amitié: figurative bond formation, not physically tying an object. The three question answers, in band order, are "formed", "lia", "lia"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Une étroite amitié describes closeness between people, not narrow physical dimensions. The three question answers, in band order, are "close", "étroite", "étroite"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The secretary and Micromégas form a close relationship as friends. The three question answers, in band order, are "friendship", "amitié", "amitié"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: À la vérité and en vérité qualify the narrator’s assertion, not a concrete truth claimed as an object. Existing published truth identity needs contextual identity review before reuse; no new mastery from spelling. The three question answers, in band order, are "in fact", "vérité", "vérité"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Rendait un fort bon compte des inventions means he reported or explained the inventions well, not returned an object. Historical Académie: https://www.dictionnaire-academie.fr/article/A4C1820 The three question answers, in band order, are "gave a good account", "rendait", "rendait"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Un bon compte des inventions is an account of others’ discoveries, not a final reckoning in the published sense. Historical Académie: https://www.dictionnaire-academie.fr/article/A4C1820 The three question answers, in band order, are "account or explanation", "compte", "compte"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Passablement de petits vers et de grands calculs counts productions, rather than judging their quality. The de + noun construction is a quantity use: https://www.dictionnaire-academie.fr/article/A9P0816 and https://www.cnrtl.fr/definition/passablement The three question answers, in band order, are "quite a few", "passablement", "passablement"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Petits vers are lines of poetry, distinct from published directional preposition vers and later directional tokens. The three question answers, in band order, are "lines of poetry", "vers", "vers"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The narrator promises to recount a conversation for his readers; not to bring back a physical object. The three question answers, in band order, are "shall recount", "rapporterai", "rapporterai"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: Pour la satisfaction des lecteurs means to give readers pleasure or gratification. Later satisfaction of needs means fulfillment, a separate contextual subset. The three question answers, in band order, are "pleasure", "satisfaction", "satisfaction"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Source sense: The narrator addresses those who read this written account. The three question answers, in band order, are "readers", "lecteurs", "lecteurs"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.

Sirius is a literal star; the same-form published questions all teach figurative luck, so retain the new celestial sense. Source sense: Sirius is literally a star. All three published questions for the same singular surface teach the figurative bonne étoile of luck, so a distinct sense is needed. The other two workwide étoile uses also name actual stars. The three question answers, in band order, are "star", "étoile", "étoile"; each choice set was checked against its own sentence context.
